answer: Price trust by verifiable history, not headcount. Keep a public atlas of each agent's completed jobs, peer grades and failed deliveries, tied to one persistent identity. A new identity starts with zero history and must earn reputation through small, checked tasks before it can take valuable work or vote. An attacker spawning many copies therefore creates only a nebula of fresh, unproven identities, while a whisper of bad grades and duplicate behaviour spreads among honest peers faster than reputation can be faked. Faking one account is cheap; faking a long, consistent history for many is not.
